current_reality.title: A burden left to the individual
current_reality.summary: The talk questions a private-machine account of the body: relationships and surroundings shape regulation, while responsibility is left with the individual. This is a source argument, not a diagnosis of a named group.

current_reality.title: When a successful intervention harms its surroundings
current_reality.summary: A target can be met while the wider living system responds in unintended ways. The causal connection is an AI inference from the talk’s account of lineal control.

current_reality.title: Whose purposes shape our attention?
current_reality.summary: Anticipatory environments can support people or narrow their agency. The script separates the cited smart-home proposal from Heath’s extension to phones and feeds.

future_reality.title: Offer a practice that people can leave
future_reality.summary: Shared rhythms and consent arrangements act together in the proposed benefit. Pressure and feeling less safe remain possible harms; an opt-out is not proof that pressure has been prevented.

future_reality.title: Let responses change the next move
future_reality.summary: Listening and retuning may support learning. What counts as useful feedback and whether the response changes anything need testing in a bounded setting.

future_reality.title: Ask whether a tool widens choices
future_reality.summary: Assessment is meant to support chosen purposes, but naming a purpose does not itself change a tool’s design or ownership. The connection remains a hypothesis.

overview.title: Arrive together, without owing the room your calm

overview.title: Body, tools and a wider world
overview.text: The talk travels through embodied cognition, predictive processing and extended minds toward a somatic commons. It distinguishes evidence for coupling, contested extension and a philosophical commitment to participation. This practical reconstruction does not require agreement that tools constitute minds. A willing group, any conflict, prerequisites, assigned actions and participant assessment still need to be established.

goal.title: Flourishing with autonomy and boundaries
goal.summary: Four proposed success factors and eight supporting conditions. Read each arrow as a necessity claim to test in a bounded community, rather than a complete recipe for flourishing.

current_reality.title: When regulation becomes an individual problem
current_reality.summary: A private-machine framing is connected to a candidate policy of individual optimisation, reduced collective support and possible isolation or unrepaired rupture. These are source-based hypotheses, not observations of a named group.

current_reality.title: When predictability displaces learning
current_reality.summary: Fixed targets can overlook wider harms, while suppressing variation may make responses brittle. The muted policy statement belongs to the preceding part; alternative causes and missing conditions remain open.

current_reality.title: Whose purposes shape attention and choice?
current_reality.summary: Adaptive tools and pressure for predictability may increase external shaping of attention. Heath’s extension to phones and feeds is her synthesis; whether that shaping narrows agency needs testing.

conflict.title: Can reliable safety coexist with shared control?
conflict.summary: Both protection from overwhelm and adaptability matter. The apparent conflict rests on an assumption that safety requires imposed individual regulation. Check whether the positions concern the same decisions and whether participatory safeguards can meet both needs.

future_reality.title: Voluntary support, with a real right to leave
future_reality.summary: Shared rhythms, consent, protected solitude and participatory safeguards jointly support the proposed route to co-regulation and repair. Settling may help some people; pressure and loss of safety remain possible. No one owes the room their calm.

future_reality.title: Tools that people can inspect, change and stop
future_reality.summary: Visibility and privacy safeguards must be backed by actual authority to change the tool. More meaningful choice is a prediction; surveillance is a possible harmful branch and privacy protection is an untested remedy.

future_reality.title: Learn from variation and revise the next move
future_reality.summary: Listening and retuning may turn surprise into learning and support adaptation. Relevant feedback may arrive across bodily, social and environmental timescales; useful uncertainty is not the same as overwhelming people.

future_reality.title: Bring support, choice and adaptability together
future_reality.summary: The three routes meet jointly in a revisable practice of being-with. The muted statements show the other parts’ outcomes; none is presented as sufficient on its own, and the joint route remains incomplete and untested.

prerequisite.title: Find a willing host and agree what matters
prerequisite.summary: Only the absence of an agreed host is established here. The other obstacles are candidates for a host to check. A group needs to make the purpose and criteria its own.

prerequisite.title: Make participation and control workable
prerequisite.summary: Usable consent and harm response, available time and repair roles, and meaningful tool control address candidate obstacles. Preparation can happen in parallel; drawing these objectives does not establish readiness.

prerequisite.title: Create shared evidence and revise together
prerequisite.summary: For this illustrative pilot, consent, resources and tool control are readiness conditions for a shared assessment. Benefits, harms and surprises need actual experience and relevant participants’ judgements.

transition.title: Map what regulates whom
transition.summary: Illustrative condition and action, not an observation or assigned task. A willing host would identify its relationships, tools and routines. Later assessments feed back into this inquiry without assuming that the original problem recurs.

transition.title: Agree the purpose and participation arrangements
transition.summary: A shared picture supports agreeing desired effects, observable criteria, consent and withdrawal. The action requires willing participants and workable arrangements, not agreement with the author’s ontology.

transition.title: Offer a small practice people can change or leave
transition.summary: With the purpose and participation arrangements in place, a host could offer an optional pause or check-in and a way to report strain. This can proceed alongside the tool review.

transition.title: Review one tool and enable practical choice
transition.summary: With the same agreed purpose, participants could inspect one tool and seek explanation, privacy protection and override. This branch does not depend on completing the shared-practice branch.

transition.title: Listen to benefits, harms and surprises, then retune
transition.summary: The illustrative branches come together for assessment. Ask what helped, harmed or surprised people and revise or stop; the cycle has no assigned owner, agreed feedback provider or recorded result.

overview.title: Flourishing with room to choose
overview.text: The goal holds autonomy and personal boundaries together with relational support. Its proposed conditions concern voluntary participation, learning from uncertainty, repair and purposes that people can question and change.
link: Inspect the goal and its supporting conditions →

overview.title: When regulation becomes an individual problem
overview.text: The map now connects the private-machine framing to individual optimisation, reduced collective support, pressure for predictability and technologies without shared control. Isolation, unrepaired rupture, brittleness and diminished agency are candidate effects to investigate.

overview.title: Enough safety and enough openness
overview.text: Protection from overwhelm and the ability to adapt are both legitimate needs. The proposed conflict asks whether sufficient safety really requires imposed individual regulation. Participatory safeguards are a possible response to that assumption.

overview.title: Support, choice and learning together
overview.text: Offer practices people can adapt or leave; make one tool contestable and reversible; act, listen and retune. These routes contribute jointly to a lived, revisable practice. Pressure to appear calm and surveillance remain possible harms; safeguards need to work in practice.
link: Inspect benefits, joint conditions and possible harms →

overview.title: Readiness belongs to a willing group
overview.text: A host must agree the situation and criteria, make consent and withdrawal usable, secure time and repair arrangements, and establish actual control over the tool. These are proposed readiness conditions, not completed preparations.
link: Review the obstacles and intermediate objectives →

overview.eyebrow: How the proposal could be tried
overview.title: Map, agree, try, listen and retune
overview.text: An illustrative sequence maps the setting and agrees a bounded purpose. A voluntary practice and a tool review can then proceed in parallel. Participants assess what helped, harmed or surprised them and revise or stop. No host, trial or owner is assigned.
link: Follow the sequence and feedback loop →

overview.title: Body, relationships and a wider world
overview.text: Heath’s talk moves through embodied cognition, predictive processing, extended minds and shared timing toward the somatic commons. Evidence for coupling, contested constitution of mind and philosophical participation remain distinct. These six views are temporary analytical cuts through reciprocal processes across timescales; they are the first bounded application, not eighteen completed maps of Body, We and World.

goal.title: Flourishing with autonomy and boundaries
goal.summary: Four proposed success factors and eight supporting conditions. Read each arrow as a necessity claim to test in a bounded community, rather than a complete recipe for flourishing.

current_reality.title: Heath’s account of process and reciprocal agency
current_reality.summary: Three attributed observations reconstruct the philosophical starting point. They have no causal connections: the practical application does not establish these claims, and the AI’s formulations await author review.

current_reality.title: When regulation becomes an individual problem
current_reality.summary: A private-machine framing is connected to a candidate policy of individual optimisation, reduced collective support and possible isolation or unrepaired rupture. These are source-based hypotheses, not observations of a named group.

current_reality.title: When predictability displaces learning
current_reality.summary: Fixed targets can overlook wider harms, while suppressing variation may make responses brittle. The muted policy statement belongs to the preceding part; alternative causes and missing conditions remain open.

current_reality.title: Whose purposes shape attention and choice?
current_reality.summary: Adaptive tools and pressure for predictability may increase external shaping of attention. Heath’s extension to phones and feeds is her synthesis; whether that shaping narrows agency needs testing.

conflict.title: Can reliable safety coexist with shared control?
conflict.summary: Both protection from overwhelm and adaptability matter. The apparent conflict rests on an assumption that safety requires imposed individual regulation. Check whether the positions concern the same decisions and whether participatory safeguards can meet both needs.

future_reality.title: Voluntary support, with a real right to leave
future_reality.summary: Shared rhythms, consent, protected solitude and participatory safeguards jointly support the proposed route to co-regulation and repair. Settling may help some people; pressure and loss of safety remain possible. No one owes the room their calm.

future_reality.title: Tools that people can inspect, change and stop
future_reality.summary: Visibility and privacy safeguards must be backed by actual authority to change the tool. More meaningful choice is a prediction; surveillance is a possible harmful branch and privacy protection is an untested remedy.

future_reality.title: How interaction can change capacities and purposes
future_reality.summary: Reciprocal adjustments may generate coordination that changes capacities, expectations and subsequent participation. Some surprise may open new meanings or purposes. Novelty can also overwhelm or harm; this is not a recommendation to increase uncertainty. The loop is an AI inference to examine in a concrete activity; timing and power remain open.

future_reality.title: Bring support, choice and adaptability together
future_reality.summary: The three routes meet jointly in a revisable practice of being-with. The muted statements show the other parts’ outcomes; none is presented as sufficient on its own, and the joint route remains incomplete and untested.

prerequisite.title: Find a willing host and agree what matters
prerequisite.summary: Only the absence of an agreed host is established here. The other obstacles are candidates for a host to check. A group needs to make the purpose and criteria its own.

prerequisite.title: Make participation and control workable
prerequisite.summary: Usable consent and harm response, available time and repair roles, and meaningful tool control address candidate obstacles. Preparation can happen in parallel; drawing these objectives does not establish readiness.

prerequisite.title: Create shared evidence and revise together
prerequisite.summary: For this illustrative pilot, consent, resources and tool control are readiness conditions for a shared assessment. Benefits, harms and surprises need actual experience and relevant participants’ judgements.

transition.title: Trace one activity through time
transition.summary: Trace how bodies, others, tools and places shape attention, coordination and available possibilities over time. The condition is illustrative, not an observation of a host; later assessment feeds back into this inquiry.

transition.title: Agree the purpose and participation arrangements
transition.summary: A shared picture supports agreeing desired effects, observable criteria, consent and withdrawal. The action requires willing participants and workable arrangements, not agreement with the author’s ontology.

transition.title: Offer a small practice people can change or leave
transition.summary: With the purpose and participation arrangements in place, a host could offer an optional pause or check-in and a way to report strain. This can proceed alongside the tool review.

transition.title: Review one tool and enable practical choice
transition.summary: With the same agreed purpose, participants could inspect one tool and seek explanation, privacy protection and override. This branch does not depend on completing the shared-practice branch.

transition.title: Review changes in capacities and purposes
transition.summary: The illustrative branches come together to ask what helped, harmed or surprised people, and what changed in their capacities or purposes. Continue, revise or stop, including reconsidering the shared purpose. No owner, feedback provider or result is assigned.

overview.title: Becoming through relationship
overview.text: Heath describes selves and capacities taking shape through ongoing relations among bodies, others, tools and environments. Agency unfolds through reciprocal activity; some uncertainty can bring forth new meanings and possibilities. These cards reconstruct her account, before the AI’s proposed practical application.
link: Follow the songline, enmindment and their sources →

overview.title: Flourishing with room to choose
overview.text: The goal holds autonomy and personal boundaries together with relational support. Its proposed conditions concern voluntary participation, learning from uncertainty, repair and purposes that people can question and change.
link: Inspect the goal and its supporting conditions →

overview.title: When regulation becomes an individual problem
overview.text: The map now connects the private-machine framing to individual optimisation, reduced collective support, pressure for predictability and technologies without shared control. Isolation, unrepaired rupture, brittleness and diminished agency are candidate effects to investigate.

overview.title: A candidate tension in this application
overview.text: Protection from overwhelm and the ability to adapt are both legitimate needs. The AI’s proposed dilemma asks whether sufficient safety requires imposed individual regulation. Its usefulness for a particular group, and its fidelity to Heath’s emphasis, remain open for review.

overview.title: Let interaction develop capacities and purposes
overview.text: Offer practices people can adapt or leave; make one tool contestable and reversible; act, listen and retune. Reciprocal coordination may change capacities and what participants seek together. Pressure to appear calm and surveillance remain possible harms; safeguards need to work in practice.
link: Inspect benefits, joint conditions and possible harms →

overview.title: Readiness belongs to a willing group
overview.text: A host must agree the situation and criteria, make consent and withdrawal usable, secure time and repair arrangements, and establish actual control over the tool. These are proposed readiness conditions, not completed preparations.

overview.eyebrow: How the proposal could be tried
overview.title: Trace, agree, try and reconsider together
overview.text: An illustrative sequence traces one activity over time and agrees an initial bounded purpose. A voluntary practice and a tool review can proceed in parallel. Participants assess benefits, harms, surprises and changes in their capacities or purposes, then continue, revise or stop. No host, trial or owner is assigned.

overview.title: A source account and one possible application
overview.text: Heath’s account of process, extended mind, timing and enmindment comes first. The six questions then explore one selected application to a bounded somatic commons. Evidence for coupling, contested constitution and philosophical participation remain distinct; neither the practical map nor its feedback loop establishes the ontology.
